primaryQuery: why do smart lights turn on after a power outage
readerQuestion: Why do smart lights come on when power returns, and what is the safest reliable way to stop them lighting up unexpectedly?
selectedBecause: This is a plain homeowner question that recurs across Reddit, Home Assistant Community, multiple lighting brands, and several years. Current search results are fragmented between single-brand instructions, community workarounds, and generic electrical explanations; they do not give readers one current cross-brand decision path from device firmware setting to controller fallback. The answer is durable, immediately useful, and a natural fit for Tara's resilient-home guidance. Search Console opportunities and the existing article inventory were reviewed before selection: Tara has proven interest in lighting and outage content but no page serving bulb power-restore intent, while the strongest camera and energy alternatives sit closer to existing high-impression Tara pages.

demandSignals.evidence: A highly engaged homeowner thread asks how to stop every light coming on after an outage and shows why reacting to every Home Assistant restart is not a dependable substitute for device settings.
A cross-platform home-automation discussion describes nursery lights waking the household when power returns, confirming a broad consumer problem rather than a Home Assistant-only symptom.
A 2025 newcomer initially asks for an automation, while the discussion points back to checking the bulb's own power-on behavior first.
Exact-query results split the answer among brand support pages, individual forum threads, and generic electrical explanations rather than one current cross-brand homeowner guide.
A current Zigbee2MQTT issue shows an exposed power-on control failing because the exact device reports the attribute as unsupported, confirming that availability must be checked model by model.

searchReview.query: why do smart lights turn on after a power outage
searchReview.intent: The reader wants a simple explanation for the surprise behavior and concrete steps that keep lights from waking the household when household power returns.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results explain one brand, one electrical cause, or one automation workaround at a time. They do not clearly distinguish the bulb's stored restore rule from a hub automation, compare the different vendor labels, warn that the first flash may happen before a controller reconnects, or preserve an ordinary wall-switch recovery path.

officialSources.name: Philips Hue iOS release notes
officialSources.supports: Hue Bridge v2 introduced configurable Power-on behavior, including returning lights to their previous state, with later controls for preferred color and brightness.

officialSources.name: Philips Hue lamp release notes
officialSources.supports: Hue documents a five-cycle manual factory reset for Bluetooth-capable lights, supporting the warning not to experiment with rapid power cycling.

officialSources.name: LIFX Light Restore documentation
officialSources.supports: LIFX distinguishes Always Turn On, Previous Power State, and the separate wall-switch Toggle Restore path, with support varying by generation and firmware.

officialSources.name: TP-Link Tapo Default State documentation
officialSources.supports: Supported Tapo lights expose Default States, where Turn On/Off restores the previous state and Turn On always illuminates after power returns.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant ZHA documentation
officialSources.supports: Many mains-powered Zigbee bulbs act as mesh routers and are intended to remain powered rather than routinely disconnected at the wall.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Network UPS Tools documentation
officialSources.supports: NUT can expose UPS status for power-event automations when the device provides it, and Home Assistant polls the NUT server every 60 seconds by default.

officialSources.name: Zigbee2MQTT Philips Hue White 75W A19 device documentation
officialSources.supports: Philips Hue model 929003856401 exposes On, Off, Toggle, and Previous power-on behavior through Zigbee2MQTT, while its Off choice removes the sequential wall-switch recovery path.

existingCoverage.decision: The existing lighting guide covers room planning, the outage articles cover controller continuity, and the commercial page owns presence-based lighting packages. None explains a bulb's firmware-level restore state, cross-brand labels, or why a controller automation can respond too late, so the new query is materially distinct.
